newsitem.title: JAPAN: Russia central banker may discuss PGMs in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Russia central banker may discuss PGMs in Japan.

text.p: A representative from Russia's central bank is expected to visit Japan from June 9, probably to negotiate the sale of platinum group metals (PGMs) to Japan, Japanese traders said on Friday.

A Russian central bank mission visited Japan in April to gather information about the Japanese precious metals market, eyeing a future role for the central bank as a seller of PGMs, but no PGM sales contracts were signed with Japanese customers at that time.
"The purpose of the visit (in June) is believed to be a follow-up of the visit in April, although it is still not clear at this stage whether we will sign an export contract," one trader said.
Meanwhile, export contract talks between the Russian PGM export agency, Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz), and Japanese clients were set for June 1 to June 11, traders said.
"There is a strong possibility that both Almaz and the Russian central bank will be able to sell PGMs," another trader said.
In the past, Almaz was Russia's sole PGM exporter.

Bureaucratic delays in Russia have prevented any export licences for PGMs from being issued so far this year, resulting in a protracted suspension of Russian PGM exports since the beginning of this year.
Japan is the world's largest PGM consumer. Russia supplies more than 60 percent of the world's palladium and about 20 percent of its platinum.
